case.summary: The case involved four online purchases of $400–$500 on card C03633-K1 within 21 minutes, totaling $1,935.29. Evidence showed the amounts were far outside the card’s normal history and matched a known fraud pattern that had appeared on 11 other cards in the same period, so the investigation concluded fraud. The card was blocked, the transaction declined, and the case was escalated to a fraud analyst for further review. The analyst confirmed the coordinated scheme and agreed the case should be filed as a SAR.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-25 21:00 and 2016-11-25 21:21, card C03633-K1 held by customer C03633 was used for 4 online transaction(s) totalling $1,935.29 (transaction IDs 3487284, 3487318, 3487340, 3487348). The activity came to the bank's attention through an analyst request on 2016-11-25 21:21:00, referring to transaction 3487348 for $477.74. The transactions were billed in region code(s) 191 (country code 87 unless noted), and the purchaser email domain was gmail.com. Online activity used the device profile MacOS | Mac OS X 10_8_5 | chrome 49.0 | 1280x800. The activity fits none of the bank's five documented fraud patterns. Authorization-threshold structuring: 4 online purchases on one card, each between $400 and $500, inside about 21 minutes, from more than one device. The amounts look chosen to stay just under a $500 authorization limit. The same run shape appears on 11 other cards in the surrounding weeks, so it is a repeated scheme across customers rather than one compromised card. The same scheme links to other cards, which have been placed under monitoring: C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06881-K1, C07297-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2. Analyst confirms the repeated under-$500 run shape links 11 other cards with the same activity in the window and agrees it is one coordinated scheme. The card has been recommended for blocking and reissue, and the total suspicious amount reported is $1,935.29.
